note: Independent re-quantisation of the pinned bf16 head (EigenLabs/Qwen3.8-27B-MTP-bf16) to 8-bit affine group-64 with MLX mx.quantize(group_size=64, bits=8), matching the backbone's uint32-packed affine layout so the scales-keyed loader walk needs no code change. The 8 2D Linear weights become packed U32 weights (4 values/word) plus bf16 scales/biases (31 tensors); the 7 1D norms stay bf16. The head only proposes; the pinned target re-verifies every emitted token against the hidden serial trajectory. sha256 is the tree digest over the single fetched model.safetensors per the documented rule; bytes is the fetched file size. Rationale vs the previous 4-bit arm: the 4-bit head traded 3.5pp acceptance (0.956 vs 0.991 bf16) for ~4.5% head-step cost. 8-bit affine g64 keeps the packed-uint32 geometry (so zero loader changes) while cutting the quantization error ~16x, buying back most of that acceptance (worst per-tensor max-abs error 7.8e-3 vs bf16 reference, loadcheck-verified through MLX affine dequantize) at roughly half the head-cost saving of the 4-bit arm. Net expectation on the h=0.18 frontier schedule: acceptance closer to bf16 (0.98+) at head cost closer to 4-bit, i.e. a positive move on the candidate/serial ratio versus both shipped heads; measured A/B pending on the local paired run (score.json).
